advances.name: Double-Entry Bookkeeping
advances.desc: Italian merchants keep two columns for every sum and always know where the money went.

advances.name: Caravels
advances.desc: Light, handy ships that beat back against the wind, so captains dare to follow the African coast south.

advances.name: Bombards
advances.desc: Great bronze guns that knock down in a week walls that held for a century.

advances.name: The Printing Press
advances.desc: Movable type turns out more books in a week than a monastery of scribes copies in a year.

advances.name: Ocean Navigation
advances.desc: The astrolabe, tables of the sun and the trade winds: captains who can find their way home from the open ocean.

advances.name: Humanist Statecraft
advances.desc: Secretaries schooled in Latin and law draft treaties, run chanceries and win over conquered towns.

advances.name: Pike and Shot
advances.desc: Squares of pikemen with handgunners on their flanks: infantry that stands against knights.

advances.name: Banking Houses
advances.desc: Bills of exchange and great family banks move money across Europe without a coin changing hands.

advances.name: Star Forts
advances.desc: Low, angled bastions of earth and brick that shrug off cannon fire.

advances.name: Scientific Cartography
advances.desc: Charts drawn to scale and courses kept true: settlers and soldiers arrive where they meant to go.

advances.name: Galleons
advances.desc: Tall, heavily gunned ships that can cross any ocean and fight when they arrive.

advances.name: Musket and Volley
advances.desc: Heavier guns fired by ranks in turn: the musket, not the pike, now decides battles.

advances.name: Joint-Stock Companies
advances.desc: Merchants pool their money in shares and send whole fleets to trade and settle beyond the seas.

advances.name: Military Drill
advances.desc: Soldiers who practise every movement by numbers keep their order under fire.

advances.name: Natural Philosophy
advances.desc: Telescopes, experiments and learned societies: knowledge tested, not inherited.

advances.name: Ships of the Line
advances.desc: Fleets that fight in a single line, every gun bearing on the enemy at once.

advances.name: Royal Bureaucracy
advances.desc: Salaried officials, written records and intendants answering only to the crown.

advances.name: Flintlock and Bayonet
advances.desc: Every musket is also a pike: the last pikemen leave the battlefield.
